name: Nurdan Bağrıaçık
bio:
Astronomer and mathematician Nurdan Bağrıaçık was born in 1978. As a child, a small red telescope given as a gift sparked her fascination with the stars and the depths of space. She studied at the Department of Astronomy and Space Sciences at Istanbul University’s Faculty of Science, alongside mathematics education. Believing that “astronomers should be beside the telescope,” she helped establish a new observatory. She also worked as a mathematics teacher.

Her love for the concept of infinity inspired her to study the universe, the brain, numbers, and musical notes at her own education center. She is the author of Little Astronomers, one of the first examples in Türkiye of the “illustrated scientific novel” genre in astronomy, with the titles The Red Telescope, Sky from an Umbrella, Friends of the Sun, and Dance of the Universe. She also wrote What Kind of PiNocchio Is This?, Flower Eclipse, The Planet That Wanted a Coat, Astronaut Season, and Equinox Dreams.
